confidence_note: Step six (generate short-term wins) and the criteria (visible, unambiguous, clearly related to the change effort), the six-to-eighteen-month window, managers planning wins into the yearly plan and rewarding people, undermining cynics, and the separate error of declaring victory too soon are consistent across secondary sources; book text itself not read. Old-text scene (six months pass, nothing concrete, cynicism spreads) and the quoted Kotter sentence are not tied to the book and were dropped.
facts: Kotter's change model has eight stages; the sixth is generating short-term wins.
A real transformation takes years; an effort with no short-term goals to meet and celebrate risks losing momentum.
Kotter says most people will not stay on the long march unless they see compelling evidence within roughly six to eighteen months that it is producing results.
Without such evidence many give up and some join the people resisting the change.
A win must be visible, unambiguous and clearly related to the change effort.

In successful transformations managers look for clear performance improvements, set them as goals in the yearly planning system, achieve them and reward the people involved with recognition, promotions, even money.
Wins give evidence to people who made sacrifices and undermine cynics and self-serving resisters.
Kotter lists failing to plan wins systematically, and declaring victory too soon, as separate errors.
scene_details: goals written into the yearly planning system
recognition, promotions, money for the people involved
tension: A long change needs proof early, but proof does not appear by itself.
opening_idea: The clock Kotter puts on people's patience.

lessons.idea: Put one visible, undisputed result early in a long project.
lessons.anchor: Kotter's win must be visible, unambiguous and tied to the change; managers plan it into the yearly plan.
lessons.everyday_example_idea: A baker switching to a new ordering system shows one branch finishing morning deliveries without gaps.

reflect_final: In a long project you are running now, which concrete result could others see next month and tie to the change?

use_cases.situation: Team tired in a long transformation
use_cases.move: Kotter wants wins planned into the yearly plan; ask which result everyone can see this month.

use_cases.situation: Employee doubts the new process works
use_cases.move: Agree to measure one small area first and look at the result together.

use_cases.situation: Starting a goal that takes years
use_cases.move: Name its first visible proof and put a date on it.

pocket_idea: A long change survives on an early result everyone can see: plan it, then celebrate it.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: Kotter gives people six to eighteen months to see proof.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: Wins are planned, visible, unambiguous and tied to the change.
